hypotheses.claim: ClayCode must distinguish serializable capability description/reference from bearer possession; a structurally forgeable CapabilityToken record cannot by itself be the authority root.
hypotheses.falsifier: A compiler/runtime design showing record-constructible tokens cannot be used to authorize without any external unforgeable state, with a proof or adversarial execution demonstrating non-forgeability.

hypotheses.claim: Type/effect checking is necessary but insufficient for execution-authority safety; every lowering/FFI/subprocess path must satisfy transitive authority closure against an external capability root.
hypotheses.falsifier: A target backend with ambient host authority that still proves every protected effect unreachable under arbitrary generated code, without relying on an external sandbox/capability boundary.

hypotheses.claim: Translation-validation receipts should bind source semantic hash, effect-manifest hash, adapter ABI/set hash, capability-scope hash, target hash and execution-environment identity so authority widening is detectable.
hypotheses.falsifier: A smaller receipt set that detects all tested authority-widening mutations with equal or stronger guarantees.

hypotheses.claim: The best first Ubuntu implementation is a two-plane ABI: EffectIntent carries only descriptive CapabilityRef/requirements; an unforgeable non-serializable host CapabilityHandle is supplied by the effect broker at execution/instantiation, not by model output.
hypotheses.falsifier: An alternative design such as signed sealed capabilities matches forge resistance, attenuation, revocation, replay and usability with lower complexity/latency.

counterhypotheses.claim: A capability record validated only by its Clay-visible fields is sufficient authority.
counterhypotheses.counterexample: 20,000/20,000 forged structural records were accepted by the deliberately structural validator.

counterhypotheses.claim: Effect intent/type declarations alone prevent authority escalation even when lowered code has ambient host access.
counterhypotheses.counterexample: 10,000/10,000 unauthorized protected-effect intents bypassed the broker in the deliberately ambient backend model.

counterhypotheses.claim: Cryptographically signed/host-validated serialized capability tokens can replace opaque runtime handles without weakening the required invariants.
counterhypotheses.next_test: Implement signed-token variant with revocation, delegation, replay resistance and disclosure model; compare complexity/latency/forge resistance against opaque handle table.

reason: Current G9 already states textual capability names never confer authority and model intent/authority are separate. The new result turns those rules into an implementation/ABI constraint. Change syntax/types only if actual compiler/runtime realization cannot enforce the split without an explicit new sealed/opaque resource kind.
